Approach

We explain the complaint before any test is booked

At Fukubi Clinic, testing serves to clarify a specific clinical problem, not to follow a routine administrative checklist. When you visit us, our physicians begin by taking a detailed personal history, discussing your everyday diet, and reviewing any previous laboratory work. In many situations, tailored dietary guidance, temporary medication, or a straightforward non-invasive breath test resolves the concern without invasive procedures.

When a gastroscopy, colonoscopy, or ultrasound is genuinely needed, we outline the exact scope of the examination, how to prepare safely, and what answers it can provide. You receive a full written estimate before scheduling, ensuring complete financial and clinical clarity before any procedure begins.

pages.title: About
pages.content:
About

About Fukubi Clinic

Founded in 2014 by Dr Lena Moravec, Fukubi Clinic provides calm, thorough outpatient care for digestive and liver conditions in Vancouver. We take time to discuss symptoms and outline diagnostic options clearly before any procedural test is scheduled.

We explain first
Two readers per report
Written estimate before tests

Our approach: we explain first

Dr Lena Moravec founded Fukubi Clinic in 2014 around a straightforward principle: patients should understand their symptoms before any procedural test is booked. During digestive appointments, anxiety often stems from uncertainty rather than discomfort alone. We prioritize unhurried clinical conversations where our physicians review medical histories, explain potential causes, and outline sensible next steps. If a diagnostic procedure like an endoscopy or ultrasound is recommended, you receive a clear explanation of what the test shows and why it is suggested. You are never pressured into immediate investigations, and every care plan is agreed upon together.

Two readers per report

Accurate diagnostic interpretation requires rigorous scrutiny. At Fukubi Clinic, every scope report is reviewed and signed off by two physicians before final conclusions are delivered. Having two independent readers ensures procedural findings and microscopic details are thoroughly verified, reducing diagnostic ambiguity. Following this review, our clinicians share and explain the complete findings directly with you in person during a dedicated follow-up consultation rather than sending an impersonal summary letter.

Written estimate before tests

Medical billing should never bring surprises. Before any procedure or investigation takes place, we issue a clear written estimate detailing exact self-pay fees in Canadian dollars. Our pricing is transparent and itemized, covering physician fees, nursing care, sedation, facility usage, and report delivery. Biopsy pathology is billed strictly at laboratory cost and outlined in advance. We believe financial transparency is essential to clinical trust, allowing you to focus entirely on your health.

Clinic

Our clinic facility

Located on the second floor at 48 Marlowe Street in Vancouver, our clinic is fully accessible via passenger lift. The facility has been designed for quiet comfort and practical outpatient flow, featuring three bright daylight consulting rooms, a dedicated endoscopy suite, and a tranquil recovery lounge equipped with four comfortable reclining chairs. Situated just a six-minute walk from Waterfront station, our setting provides a calm and orderly environment from initial check-in through post-procedure recovery.

pages.title: Symptoms
pages.content:
Symptoms

Symptoms & When to Seek Care

Digestive symptoms can range from occasional discomfort to chronic disruptions that affect your daily routine. We investigate underlying causes methodically, starting with careful conversation rather than unnecessary procedural interventions.

Heartburn & reflux
Stomach pain
Bloating & gas
Changed bowel habits
Blood in the stool
Trouble swallowing
Abnormal liver tests

Urgent warning: symptoms requiring emergency care

Certain acute digestive symptoms demand immediate hospital care rather than an outpatient clinic appointment. If you experience vomiting blood, passing black or tarry stools, or sudden severe abdominal pain, go to the nearest emergency department immediately and do not book an outpatient clinic visit. These warning signs may indicate acute internal bleeding or serious intra-abdominal emergencies that require urgent hospital stabilization. For non-emergency symptoms, our outpatient clinic provides scheduled evaluations.

Heartburn and reflux

Persistent acid reflux or heartburn typically occurs when stomach acid travels upward into the esophagus, causing a burning sensation behind the breastbone or sour regurgitation. While occasional reflux is common, frequent symptoms can irritate esophageal tissues and disrupt sleep. You should come in sooner if over-the-counter remedies fail, pain radiates toward your back, or symptoms persist for weeks. We usually begin by reviewing dietary triggers, sleep posture, and medication use before determining whether an upper gastroscopy or H. pylori breath test is warranted.

Stomach pain

Localized or generalized abdominal discomfort can stem from gastric inflammation, peptic ulceration, functional dyspepsia, or biliary issues. Understanding the timing, location, and relationship of your pain to meals helps narrow down the origin. You should schedule an evaluation sooner if discomfort wakes you at night, recurs steadily, or is accompanied by unexplained appetite loss. In your first visit, our physicians perform an abdominal physical examination and review your medical history, followed by recommendations for ultrasound imaging or endoscopy when appropriate.

Bloating and gas

Excessive abdominal fullness, distension, and uncomfortable flatulence frequently indicate altered gut motility, dietary intolerances, or microbial imbalances within the digestive tract. If bloating is persistent, progressively worsens throughout the day, or interferes with regular eating habits, clinical guidance is recommended. We start with a detailed dietary review conducted alongside our registered dietitian, Tomás Reyes, and may recommend non-invasive testing such as a breath test for small intestinal bacterial overgrowth before considering any invasive procedural options.

Changed bowel habits

Noticeable shifts in bowel patterns—including ongoing diarrhea, newly developed constipation, or alternating frequency—warrant careful medical evaluation. While stress and dietary changes can temporarily affect digestion, persistent irregularities that last longer than several weeks should not be overlooked. You should seek an evaluation promptly if bowel changes are accompanied by unintended weight loss or fever. We evaluate your routine through a dedicated symptom diary and determine whether stool screening, laboratory tests, or a colonoscopy are appropriate.

Blood in the stool

Seeing bright red blood on toilet paper or mixed within stool can be unsettling. While hemorrhoids or minor anal fissures are frequent benign causes, rectal bleeding can also indicate polyps, diverticular disease, or inflammatory bowel conditions. You should book an appointment promptly for any recurring or unexplained bleeding, while heavy bleeding requires immediate emergency care. Our physicians examine the perianal area and typically recommend an unhurried colonoscopy to visualize the colonic lining directly and identify the bleeding source.

Trouble swallowing

Difficulty swallowing, medically termed dysphagia, occurs when food or liquids feel lodged in the throat or chest during transit. This symptom should never be ignored, particularly if it worsens progressively from solid foods to soft textures or liquids. You should seek clinical attention promptly if swallowing causes coughing, choking, or involuntary weight loss. During your consultation, we assess the timeline of your symptoms and typically arrange an upper gastroscopy to inspect the esophagus for inflammation, strictures, or mucosal narrowing.

Abnormal liver tests

Elevated liver enzymes identified on routine blood work—such as ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, or bilirubin—often indicate liver inflammation, fatty liver disease, metabolic factors, or medication effects. Because early liver conditions rarely produce noticeable physical symptoms, elevated lab markers require structured clinical investigation. You should schedule an appointment promptly if your doctor notes recurring abnormal values. Dr Samuel Achebe leads our liver clinic, evaluating underlying metabolic factors, medication histories, and coordinating abdominal ultrasound scans to assess liver architecture thoroughly.

pages.title: First visit
pages.content:
First visit

Your First Visit

We design your initial appointment to be calm, thorough, and unhurried. Over forty-five minutes, our clinical team focuses on understanding your medical history and planning diagnostic steps collaboratively.

Forty-five minutes

0–10 minReceptionForms, medication list, the symptom diary if you have one.
10–35 minPhysicianThe story, the examination, and what we think it is.
35–45 minNurseIf a test helps: the written estimate, a date and the fasting window.
Follow-upResultsFindings and biopsy reports explained in person, never by letter.

Step 1: Reception and check-in (0 to 10 minutes)

Upon arriving at our second-floor clinic at 48 Marlowe Street, you are welcomed by our patient coordinator, Hana Lindgren, at the reception desk. During the first ten minutes, we confirm your registration details and collect your background health information. Please provide your completed intake forms, your current medication list, and your symptom diary if you have maintained one. Gathering this documentation at check-in ensures your physician has immediate access to your medication dosages and symptom timelines before entering the consulting room.

Step 2: Consultation with your physician (10 to 35 minutes)

The central portion of your visit is spent in a quiet daylight consulting room with Dr Lena Moravec, Dr Samuel Achebe, or Dr Priya Raman. Over twenty-five minutes, your doctor listens to your clinical story, reviews the chronology of your symptoms, conducts an abdominal physical examination, and discusses potential underlying causes. We explain what your symptoms may indicate and explore diagnostic options together. We never book procedures without first ensuring you understand their purpose, clinical necessity, and potential findings.

Step 3: Preparation guidance with our nurse (35 to 45 minutes)

If an endoscopy, breath test, or ultrasound is mutually agreed upon, you spend the final ten minutes with our endoscopy nurse lead, Ines Carvalho. Nurse Carvalho reviews procedural preparation in detail, explaining your specific fasting window and medication adjustments. You receive a clear, printed schedule along with an itemized written estimate detailing all self-pay fees in Canadian dollars. Having dedicated time with our nursing staff ensures all practical questions regarding preparation and transportation are answered before you leave.

Step 4: After your visit and in-person results

When diagnostic tests or tissue biopsies are performed, results are never delivered casually by letter or brief telephone call. Biopsy pathology is processed within forty-eight hours of arriving from the laboratory, and two physicians review every endoscopic report. We schedule a dedicated twenty-minute follow-up consultation ($90 CAD) where your physician presents the written findings, explains macroscopic and microscopic observations directly, and works with you to establish an individualized ongoing treatment or dietary management plan.

What to bring to your consultation

To make the most of your forty-five-minute initial consultation ($180 CAD), please bring government-issued photo identification, a complete list of your prescription medications and supplements, and any recent laboratory or diagnostic imaging reports. If you have kept a diary recording food intake or symptom flare-ups, bring it along for review. Please arrive ten minutes prior to your scheduled appointment. Note that last check-in is strictly thirty minutes before clinic closure.

pages.title: Tests & endoscopy
pages.content:
Tests

Diagnostic Tests & Endoscopy

We provide precise outpatient gastrointestinal investigations in a modern, calm environment. Every procedural test is explained in advance with a transparent written estimate and interpreted by two independent physician readers.

Gastroscopy
Colonoscopy
Breath test
Abdominal ultrasound

Gastroscopy (upper endoscopy)

A gastroscopy evaluates the lining of the esophagus, stomach, and duodenum using a thin, flexible endoscope equipped with an illuminated camera. The procedure takes approximately 15 minutes and is performed under conscious sedation to ensure complete physical comfort. Gastroscopy is scheduled during our scope mornings on Tuesday, Thursday, or Saturday. Fasting is essential: you must consume no solid food after midnight, with clear fluids allowed until 6:00, arriving at 7:30. The fee is $520 CAD, which includes sedation, dual physician interpretation, and a complete written report. Biopsies, if required, are billed at cost.

Colonoscopy

Colonoscopy provides a detailed visual examination of the large intestine and rectum to screen for polyps, inflammation, or structural sources of altered bowel habits. The examination takes approximately 30 minutes under conscious sedation administered by our clinical team. Colonoscopies take place on Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday mornings. Full bowel preparation using our clinic-provided prep kit is mandatory, with solid foods stopped at midnight and clear liquids discontinued at 6:00 before your 7:30 arrival. The fee is $780 CAD, covering the preparation kit, sedation, two readers per report, and a post-procedure consultation.

Breath test (H. pylori and SIBO)

Breath testing is a simple, non-invasive method used to diagnose Helicobacter pylori infection or small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO). You breathe into collection bags at set intervals after consuming a specialized substrate solution, allowing us to measure exhaled gases accurately. The test takes approximately 60 minutes and requires no sedation. Patients must fast from solid food and fluids as directed prior to testing. The fee is $140 CAD, which includes test administration, immediate analysis, and a comprehensive explanation of your results with practical treatment recommendations.

Abdominal ultrasound

Abdominal ultrasound uses high-frequency sound waves to capture real-time images of the liver, gallbladder, pancreas, kidneys, and spleen without ionizing radiation. The scan takes approximately 20 minutes to complete, during which a probe is gently guided across the abdomen. No sedation is required, but fasting for six hours beforehand ensures clear visibility of abdominal organs. The fee is $220 CAD, encompassing the complete diagnostic scan and a same-day clinical explanation from your physician, allowing rapid evaluation of upper abdominal pain or abnormal liver blood tests.

Scope mornings and procedural scheduling

All endoscopic examinations at Fukubi Clinic take place exclusively on Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday mornings between 8:00 and 12:30. Concentrating procedures on these dedicated mornings allows our clinical and nursing teams to maintain focused procedural care and personalized monitoring in our recovery lounge. Patients undergoing endoscopy must observe strict fasting: no solid food after midnight and only clear fluids until 6:00, arriving promptly at 7:30. Because conscious sedation is administered, you must arrange for an adult companion to accompany you home.

pages.title: Preparation
pages.content:
Preparation

Preparation & Fasting Guidelines

Proper preparation is critical for safe sedation and clear endoscopic visualization. Please follow these structured dietary steps and fasting timelines carefully before your scheduled morning procedure.

Your fasting window

Scope mornings are Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday. Nothing to eat after midnight, clear fluids until 6:00, and arrival at 7:30. Rings mark the scope mornings.

Step by step

3 daysDietThree days before your procedure. Beginning three days prior to your colonoscopy, switch to a low-fibre diet to reduce indigestible residue within the bowel. Avoid whole grains, nuts, seeds, raw vegetables, dried fruits, pulses, and tough meats. Choose white rice, refined white bread, skinless poultry, eggs, well-cooked fish, and clear broths instead. Eliminating high-fibre foods well in advance ensures that subsequent cleansing agents work efficiently, giving our physicians unobstructed visualization of the mucosal lining and preventing the need to repeat the procedure.
18:00Prep doseThe evening before at 18:00. At 18:00 on the evening before your scheduled scope morning, take your first dose of the bowel preparation kit exactly as outlined on your printed instruction sheet. Dissolve the sachet into the measured water volume and drink the solution steadily alongside additional recommended clear fluids. You may experience bowel evacuation shortly after taking the solution. Remain near bathroom facilities throughout the evening, stay well hydrated with water or clear apple juice, and do not consume any solid food after starting the solution.
MidnightFastingMidnight: complete cessation of solid food. From midnight onwards, you must stop consuming all solid foods entirely. This strict rule applies to both gastroscopy and colonoscopy patients scheduled for morning procedures on Tuesday, Thursday, or Saturday. Having an entirely empty stomach is an indispensable safety requirement for conscious sedation, as it prevents gastric contents from entering the respiratory airway during the procedure. Any solid food consumed after midnight will necessitate immediate postponement of your scheduled endoscopy for your personal clinical safety.
6:00FluidsMorning of procedure: 6:00 fluids cutoff. On the morning of your procedure, you may sip modest quantities of clear fluids—such as plain water or clear diluted apple juice—until precisely 6:00. After 6:00, absolute fasting begins: do not drink any fluids, sip water, chew gum, or consume breath mints. If you take essential morning prescription medications, discuss them in advance with Nurse Carvalho; approved medications should be taken before 6:00 with a minimal sip of water. Adhering strictly to this fluid timeline ensures your procedure proceeds on schedule.
7:30ArrivalArrival at the clinic at 7:30. Arrive promptly at 7:30 on the second floor of 48 Marlowe Street for your scope morning appointment. Our reception coordinator, Hana Lindgren, will check you in and guide you to our clinical preparation suite. Endoscopy nurse lead Ines Carvalho will review your fasting timeline, verify your vital signs, and confirm that your companion's contact details are recorded. Arriving at 7:30 provides ample time for intravenous cannulation and pre-sedation checks without rushing before your scheduled examination begins.
AfterRecoveryAfter the examination: recovery and escort home. Following your gastroscopy or colonoscopy, you will rest comfortably in our dedicated recovery lounge, which is furnished with four private reclining chairs. You will be served warm tea and a light snack while our nursing team monitors your post-sedation recovery. Because conscious sedation temporarily impairs reflexes and judgment, you are legally prohibited from driving or operating machinery for twenty-four hours. A responsible adult companion must escort you home from the clinic; leaving unaccompanied by public transit or taxi is strictly prohibited.

Afterwards

Rest, tea, and someone to take you home

After a scope you rest in the daylight recovery lounge. Please arrange an adult to take you home: sedation stays in the body for several hours.

pages.title: Physicians & team
pages.content:
Team

Physicians & Clinical Team

Our multidisciplinary clinical team in Vancouver combines clinical expertise in gastroenterology, hepatology, nursing, and clinical nutrition. We work together to ensure every patient receives unhurried, collaborative care.

Dr Lena Moravec

Founder and Endoscopy Lead

Dr Lena Moravec founded Fukubi Clinic in 2014 with a clear vision: to establish an outpatient digestive practice where medical procedures are preceded by genuine explanation and shared understanding. As a specialist gastroenterologist and our endoscopy lead, Dr Moravec oversees clinical governance across our endoscopy suite and performs upper gastroscopies and colonoscopies. She personally co-reads every endoscopic report produced at the clinic, ensuring that findings and therapeutic recommendations are consistently validated by two physician readers before being discussed with patients.

Dr Samuel Achebe

Hepatologist and Liver Clinic Lead

Dr Samuel Achebe leads our dedicated liver clinic, focusing on the diagnosis, management, and long-term monitoring of hepatic conditions. His clinical practice addresses abnormal liver blood tests, metabolic fatty liver disease, viral hepatitis, and cirrhosis management. Dr Achebe works closely with our diagnostic imaging team to coordinate abdominal ultrasound scans, evaluating hepatic parenchyma and vascular structures. He emphasizes clear communication, explaining complex metabolic pathways and lifestyle modifications so patients understand the evidence behind their clinical recommendations.

Dr Priya Raman

Gastroenterologist

Dr Priya Raman is a specialist gastroenterologist with clinical interests in acid reflux, irritable bowel syndrome, and inflammatory bowel diseases such as Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. Dr Raman conducts initial consultations, diagnostic endoscopies, and follow-up reviews. She focuses on identifying underlying drivers of altered bowel habits and chronic dyspepsia through methodical evaluation rather than reflex procedural testing. Dr Raman works in close partnership with our registered dietitian, integrating dietary modifications with targeted pharmacological therapies to restore gut function.

Ines Carvalho

Endoscopy Nurse Lead

Ines Carvalho leads our nursing team and oversees all procedural preparation, conscious sedation monitoring, and recovery care at Fukubi Clinic. Nurse Carvalho meets with patients during the final segment of their first consultation to explain fasting schedules, bowel preparation regimens, and sedation protocols. On scope mornings, she coordinates patient intake and supervises our four-chair recovery lounge, ensuring that individuals wake comfortably and safely. Her meticulous approach to preparation minimizes procedural complications and ensures high-quality bowel cleansing for accurate mucosal visualization.

Tomás Reyes

Registered Dietitian

Tomás Reyes provides clinical dietary counseling for patients experiencing digestive discomfort, bloating, irritable bowel syndrome, and food intolerances. During fifty-minute consultation sessions ($110 CAD), Tomás analyzes detailed food diaries alongside symptom records to pinpoint nutritional triggers and optimize gut health. Rather than recommending restrictive or unverified elimination diets, he designs evidence-based, balanced dietary plans that address symptoms while maintaining nutritional adequacy, working in close communication with Dr Moravec and Dr Raman.

Hana Lindgren

Patient Coordinator

Hana Lindgren manages reception and patient coordination at Fukubi Clinic, serving as the welcoming point of contact for appointments, scheduling, and inquiries. Hana assists patients with registration paperwork, coordinates written estimates and billing details, and manages diagnostic appointment bookings across our clinic calendar. Her orderly coordination ensures that appointment times run punctually and that patients receive timely reminders regarding fasting windows, required documentation, and transit directions to our second-floor clinic on Marlowe Street.

Consultation fees and medical reviews

Initial consultations at Fukubi Clinic are scheduled for 45 minutes at a self-pay fee of $180 CAD. This comprehensive session includes a detailed medical history review, an abdominal examination, and a mutually agreed written care plan. Follow-up consultations run for 20 minutes at $90 CAD, dedicated to reviewing diagnostic findings in person and assessing ongoing treatment progress. For patients requiring specialized nutritional support, a 50-minute consultation with our registered dietitian, Tomás Reyes, is available for $110 CAD, covering food diary analysis and an individualized dietary plan.

Endoscopy fees: gastroscopy and colonoscopy

Procedural endoscopy fees are structured to cover complete clinical and facility services without unexpected extras. A gastroscopy costs $520 CAD and includes conscious sedation, dual physician interpretation, and a detailed written report. A colonoscopy is priced at $780 CAD, covering the specialized bowel preparation kit, sedation, two physician readers per report, and post-procedure recovery care. If tissue biopsies or polyp removals are clinically necessary during your procedure, pathology laboratory analysis is billed strictly at cost and clearly itemized on your written invoice.

Diagnostic test fees: breath testing and ultrasound

Non-invasive diagnostic investigations are priced clearly with same-day or expedited clinician review included. A breath test for Helicobacter pylori or small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) is $140 CAD, encompassing test administration, chemical analysis, and physician interpretation. An abdominal ultrasound examination is $220 CAD, which includes a comprehensive diagnostic scan of the upper abdominal organs and a same-day explanation of findings by your attending physician. All fees are quoted in Canadian dollars with no hidden equipment or booking surcharges.

Written estimates and insurance coverage

Financial clarity is fundamental to our clinical practice. Following your initial consultation, if any diagnostic test or endoscopic procedure is recommended, Nurse Carvalho provides an itemized written estimate before booking. As an outpatient private clinic, services are provided on a self-pay basis in Canadian dollars. While we do not bill insurance carriers directly, we provide official itemized receipts containing standard diagnostic and medical procedure codes that you may submit to your extended private health insurance carrier for potential reimbursement.

Cancellation and rescheduling policy

We schedule substantial time blocks for every consultation and procedural appointment to maintain an unhurried clinical environment. If you need to cancel or reschedule your appointment, we require a minimum of 48 hours' notice prior to your scheduled time. Cancellations received with at least 48 hours' advance notice incur no fee whatsoever. Late cancellations made within 48 hours or missed appointments may be subject to a cancellation fee, as that dedicated procedural or consultation time cannot easily be reassigned to other patients.

pages.title: FAQ
pages.content:
FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

Here are answers to common questions about appointments, procedural preparation, sedation, and receiving your results at Fukubi Clinic. If you have additional inquiries, our team is happy to assist.

Booking
Fasting & preparation
Sedation
Results

Booking

Do I need a doctor's referral to book a first visit?

No referral is required to schedule an initial consultation at Fukubi Clinic. Patients experiencing digestive symptoms, reflux, changed bowel habits, or abnormal liver blood tests may contact us directly to arrange an appointment. However, if your family physician has provided referral notes, previous laboratory findings, or recent imaging reports, please bring them along to your first visit. Having access to previous investigations helps our medical team understand your health history and avoids unnecessary duplication of prior medical tests.

How do I schedule an appointment at Fukubi Clinic?

You can schedule an appointment by calling our reception desk at +1 604 555 0148 or emailing hello@fukubi-clinic.example. Our patient coordinator, Hana Lindgren, will assist you in selecting a convenient time for your initial forty-five-minute consultation. We see patients Monday through Friday, with morning sessions from 8:00 to 12:30 and afternoon sessions from 14:00 to 18:30, excluding Wednesday and Friday afternoons when our clinic is closed for procedural reviews. Last appointment check-in is thirty minutes before closing.

What is your appointment cancellation policy?

We require a minimum of 48 hours' notice if you need to reschedule or cancel any consultation or procedural booking. Cancellations submitted with at least 48 hours' notice are entirely free of charge. Because our clinic reserves forty-five-minute consultation blocks and dedicated endoscopy suite time for each patient, short-notice cancellations within 48 hours prevent other patients from accessing care. Please contact our reception desk by telephone or email as soon as your schedule changes to avoid late fees.

Are your medical and endoscopic services covered by private insurance?

Fukubi Clinic operates as a self-pay clinic, with all fees established in Canadian dollars. We do not bill private insurance companies directly. However, after your consultation or procedure is completed and payment is processed, we issue an itemized official receipt detailing physician credentials, medical codes, and clinical services rendered. Many patients successfully submit these itemized receipts to their extended private health insurance plans or employer health spending accounts for full or partial expense reimbursement.

Fasting & preparation

When do I need to begin fasting before an endoscopy?

For all morning endoscopy procedures on Tuesday, Thursday, or Saturday, you must consume no solid food after midnight prior to your appointment. Clear fluids—such as plain water or strained apple juice—are allowed until exactly 6:00 on the morning of your procedure. After 6:00, you must consume nothing at all, including water, coffee, chewing gum, or mints. Arrive at the clinic at 7:30 with an entirely empty stomach to ensure safe sedation and clear visualization.

Why must I switch to a low-fibre diet three days before a colonoscopy?

A low-fibre diet is necessary because dietary fibre from vegetables, seeds, grains, and fruits leaves persistent residue in the colon that bowel cleansing solutions cannot fully eliminate. Starting a low-fibre diet three days prior ensures the bowel walls are thoroughly cleared of debris during your preparation. Clear mucosal surfaces allow our endoscopists to spot small flat polyps or early mucosal inflammation that might otherwise remain hidden beneath residual matter, ensuring the highest possible diagnostic accuracy during your examination.

Can I take my regular prescription medications on the morning of a procedure?

Most essential prescription medications, particularly those for high blood pressure, heart conditions, or seizure management, should be taken before 6:00 on your procedure morning with a small sip of water. However, blood-thinning medications, anticoagulants, and diabetic drugs require specific scheduling adjustments that Nurse Carvalho will outline during your preparatory consultation. Never discontinue prescribed medications without explicit clinical instructions from our team. Please bring a complete written list of your medications to your visit for review.

What should I do if I feel nauseated while drinking the bowel prep solution?

Mild nausea is a common reaction when consuming high volumes of bowel preparation liquid. If you begin to feel nauseated, pause drinking for twenty to thirty minutes to allow your stomach to settle. Walking around slowly, sucking on a clear hard candy, or drinking the solution chilled through a straw can significantly improve tolerance. Once the sensation eases, resume drinking the solution at a slower, steady pace until the entire prescribed volume is completed as directed.

Sedation

What type of sedation is used during endoscopic procedures?

At Fukubi Clinic, we use conscious sedation administered intravenously by our experienced medical team. Conscious sedation induces a state of deep relaxation, drowsiness, and physical ease, significantly reducing anxiety and discomfort while allowing you to breathe independently and respond to simple verbal cues. Most patients feel relaxed throughout the entire procedure and have little to no memory of the examination afterward. Our nursing staff continuously monitors your vital signs, oxygenation, and heart rhythm throughout the procedure.

Why must someone escort me home after conscious sedation?

Sedative medications remain in your bloodstream for several hours after your procedure, temporarily impairing your coordination, reflexes, reasoning, and depth perception. Even if you feel alert and awake in our recovery lounge, you are legally considered impaired. For your safety, clinic regulations strictly require that a responsible adult companion meet you at the clinic and accompany you home. You are not permitted to drive a motor vehicle, operate dangerous machinery, or leave unaccompanied via taxi or public transit.

Will I feel pain or discomfort during a gastroscopy or colonoscopy?

Under conscious sedation, the majority of patients experience no significant pain during either gastroscopy or colonoscopy. For gastroscopy, a mild throat spray numbs the back of your mouth to ease passage of the endoscope, preventing gagging sensations. During colonoscopy, gentle carbon dioxide insufflation is used to expand the bowel, which may occasionally cause temporary sensations of mild pressure or cramping. Our physicians and nurses work gently to minimize discomfort, adjusting sedation levels whenever necessary to ensure you remain comfortable.

Results

When and how will I receive the results of my endoscopy?

Preliminary findings are shared with you verbally before you leave our recovery lounge once sedation has worn off. However, we never deliver formal diagnostic results solely by brief letter or automated email. Instead, we arrange a dedicated twenty-minute follow-up consultation ($90 CAD) where your physician presents your complete written report, reviews printed high-definition endoscopic images with you, explains any biopsy results, and discusses an individualized treatment or dietary management plan.

Why does every scope report require two physician readers?

At Fukubi Clinic, every scope report is independently reviewed and signed by two physicians before final clinical conclusions are reached. Dual interpretation ensures that visual findings, mucosal patterns, and anatomical landmarks are evaluated with objective rigor. Having two specialist gastroenterologists review procedural imagery and microscopic findings minimizes the risk of overlooked pathology, resolves diagnostic subtleties, and provides you with the highest level of clinical certainty regarding your gastrointestinal health.

How long does it take to receive biopsy pathology reports?

If tissue biopsies or polyps are removed during your endoscopy, samples are sent immediately to an accredited pathology laboratory for microscopic analysis. Under clinic policy, our physicians complete your final diagnostic report within 48 hours of receiving pathology results from the laboratory. Once both physicians have reviewed and co-signed the comprehensive report, our reception team contacts you to confirm your follow-up consultation, where your doctor explains the findings in full clinical context.

pages.title: Contact & hours
pages.content:
Contact

Contact & Clinic Hours

Fukubi Clinic is conveniently located on the second floor of 48 Marlowe Street in Vancouver. We welcome inquiries by phone or email to assist with scheduling, directions, and procedural preparation.

Clinic hours

Fukubi Clinic is open Monday through Saturday with structured morning and afternoon clinical sessions. Morning hours run from 8:00 to 12:30 on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday for consultations, while Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday mornings are reserved exclusively for endoscopic procedures. Afternoon consultations take place from 14:00 to 18:30 on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday. The clinic is closed on Wednesday afternoons, Saturday afternoons, Sundays, and public holidays. Last check-in for all appointments is thirty minutes prior to closing time.

Clinic address and location

Our clinic is located on the second floor at 48 Marlowe Street, Vancouver, BC V6B 2K9, Canada. The building is equipped with an elevator lift providing full step-free accessibility to our second-floor reception, consultation suites, and endoscopy facilities. When you arrive, please check in with our patient coordinator, Hana Lindgren, who will verify your documentation and notify your attending physician. Please remember that last patient check-in takes place thirty minutes before session closure.

Transit access and parking information

Fukubi Clinic is conveniently situated for patients traveling by public transit, located just a six-minute walk from Waterfront station, which connects SkyTrain lines, SeaBus services, and West Coast Express trains. Several major bus routes also stop within two blocks of our Marlowe Street entrance. Please note that our clinic does not provide on-site patient parking. Visitors arriving by private car can use commercial public parking lots located two blocks away, or metered street parking along surrounding streets.

Inquiries and appointment bookings

To schedule an initial forty-five-minute consultation, adjust an existing booking, or ask questions regarding procedural preparation, contact our administration team by telephone at +1 604 555 0148 or by email at hello@fukubi-clinic.example. Our team responds promptly during regular clinic opening hours. When calling, please have your calendar and current medication list available so we can coordinate your appointment and provide your preparatory instructions smoothly.

posts.title: How to read your colonoscopy report
posts.excerpt: Understanding the clinical terminology, anatomical landmarks, and dual-physician findings in your written colonoscopy report helps you take an active role in your digestive health.
posts.content:
When your colonoscopy is completed at Fukubi Clinic, you do not simply receive an automated letter with a brief checkmark. Instead, you receive a detailed, comprehensive written report that has been independently reviewed and signed by two specialist physicians. While medical terminology can seem unfamiliar at first glance, each section of the report follows an orderly structure designed to document anatomical observations, mucosal health, and procedural safety.

At Fukubi Clinic, founded in Vancouver in 2014, our commitment to diagnostic accuracy is reflected in our policy of having two physicians independently read every endoscopic report. Dr Lena Moravec, Dr Samuel Achebe, and Dr Priya Raman review procedural recordings and photographic documentation together. This dual-reader protocol ensures that subtle mucosal irregularities, minute vascular changes, and polyp margins are examined from multiple clinical perspectives. By eliminating single-observer bias, we provide patients with an exceptionally thorough evaluation before any treatment decisions are finalized.

The opening section of your report outlines procedural details, including the duration of the examination, the conscious sedation administered, and the quality of bowel preparation. In gastroenterology, bowel preparation is categorized using validated clinical scales. A clean, unobstructed preparation allows our endoscopists to inspect the entire colonic mucosa with high diagnostic confidence. The report also notes the anatomical endpoint reached during the examination—typically the cecum or terminal ileum—confirming that the full length of the large intestine was visualized.

The central part of the report documents macroscopic findings observed along each anatomical segment, moving from the cecum through the ascending, transverse, descending, and sigmoid colon down to the rectum. If the tissue appears smooth, pale pink, and normally vascularized, the report describes the mucosa as unremarkable or normal. If areas of inflammation, diverticular outpouchings, or polyps are observed, the report specifies their exact location, estimated size in millimeters, and morphological appearance.

When polyps are detected, our physicians remove them during the procedure using specialized endoscopic instruments. The report details the removal technique applied and notes that the tissue was collected for histological analysis. Pathological evaluation examines the cells under a microscope to determine the polyp type, such as hyperplastic or adenomatous tissue. At Fukubi Clinic, biopsy pathology is billed at laboratory cost, and our physicians complete your final diagnostic report within 48 hours of receiving pathology results from the laboratory.

The final section of your report contains the clinical summary and collaborative recommendations formulated by Dr Lena Moravec and our physician team. This synthesis connects the visual findings and pathology with your reported symptoms, whether you presented with changed bowel habits, unexplained abdominal discomfort, or routine screening requirements. Rather than leaving you to interpret these conclusions alone, we review the full report together during a dedicated twenty-minute follow-up consultation.

During this in-person review, your doctor shows you the high-definition images captured during your procedure, explains what each observation means for your ongoing wellness, and outlines surveillance intervals or dietary adjustments. If nutritional strategies are beneficial, we coordinate care with our registered dietitian, Tomás Reyes. Taking time to understand your colonoscopy report provides lasting clarity, transforming technical findings into an informed, practical plan for your long-term digestive care.

posts.title: Low-fibre days before a colonoscopy
posts.excerpt: What to eat, and what to leave out, in the three days before a colonoscopy.
posts.content:
Three days before your colonoscopy, choose white bread, plain rice, eggs, fish and well-cooked vegetables without skins.

Leave out seeds, nuts, raw salad and whole grains. Our dietitian Tomás Reyes can adapt the list for allergies.

On the evening before, you take the first preparation dose at 18:00 as written on your sheet.

posts.title: Breath tests are back on Wednesdays
posts.excerpt: Non-invasive breath tests for H. pylori and SIBO are available again on Wednesday mornings.
posts.content:
Breath tests are quick, non-invasive and need no sedation. They are available again on Wednesday mornings from 8:00.

The test costs $140, which includes the clinical explanation of the result.

Please avoid antibiotics for four weeks and fast for eight hours beforehand.

posts.title: Holiday hours, 24 Dec–2 Jan
posts.excerpt: The clinic closes from 24 December and reopens on 2 January; here is how to reach us in between.
posts.content:
The clinic is closed from 24 December and reopens on 2 January.

Your family doctor or the nearest emergency department can help with urgent symptoms.

Reception answers messages by email on weekdays during the closure.

posts.title: What the recovery lounge is for
posts.excerpt: The daylight lounge with four reclining chairs is where you rest after sedation, with someone beside you.
posts.content:
After a scope you rest in our daylight recovery lounge, which has four reclining chairs and a window onto the street.

A nurse checks in with you while the sedation settles, and a companion is welcome to sit beside you.

Most people go home within the hour; someone should take you home and stay with you until the evening.
